about.pitch: Stamps the time, date, weekday, address and a tracking code onto your photos — for field records, site inspections and proof of service.
about.privacyGeocoding: When GPS is used, the operating system sends the coordinate to Google’s or Apple’s map service to obtain the address. That is the only information that leaves here, and it is the system that sends it, not Lymark.
about.privacyLocation: Location is used once per capture, only to fill in the address field, and is not stored separately from the photos.
about.privacyOnDevice: The photos, the addresses and the history stay on this device alone. The account exists for your subscription: the server keeps your e-mail and plan, and never receives your photos or your location.
about.title: About Lymark

watermark.backdropBandNote: The band runs edge to edge across the photo and rests against the margin where the stamp is anchored. Over a busy scene — a building site, a yard, a crowded façade — it reads as the document’s caption rather than a sticker placed on top.
watermark.backdropBlockNote: The backing follows the size of the text, with padding around it.
watermark.backdropDescription: Keeps contrast over light areas of the photo. Without it, the text sits directly on the image, with a shadow.
watermark.brandDescription: Above the clock it becomes a signature, with logo and tagline. In a corner, it is a discreet line.
watermark.brandNote: Leave the second part empty for a single-colour mark. A long name is shrunk until it fits, rather than cut off.
watermark.codeDescription: On the side it does not compete for room with the picture itself.
watermark.colorsDescription: The colour on the photo is the company’s choice, not the app’s — changing it here does not change the screen colours.
watermark.cornerConflict: The mark and the data are in the same corner — they will overlap on the photo.
watermark.fieldsDescription: Only the fields that are on and have content reach the photo.
watermark.includeCountryDescription: Turn it on if you work across borders. Otherwise it only takes room on the photo.
watermark.logoAdded: Logo added to the brand header.
watermark.logoAlignNote: The logo height follows the text: its top aligns with the top of the name and its bottom with the baseline of the tagline.
watermark.logoErrorMessage: Try another image. A PNG with a transparent background is the format that works best.
watermark.logoErrorTitle: This file could not be used
watermark.logoFormatNote: Use a PNG with a transparent background. A JPG with a white background becomes a white rectangle on the photo — the format does not store transparency, and the app has no way of guessing what is background.
watermark.logoPermissionMessage: Allow it in Settings › Permissions to choose the logo file.
watermark.positionDescription: The corner of the photo the block is anchored to.
watermark.previewCurrent: Over the current photo from the Capture tab.
watermark.previewEmpty: From light to dark, to check legibility at both extremes.
watermark.previewNoFields: No field selected — the photo comes out without a watermark.

availability.description: Lymark is at version 1.3.0, in testing on Android ahead of publication on Google Play. There is no iOS version and no web version, and the app collects no payment.
availability.title: Availability

device.description: The account exists for your subscription: the server keeps your e-mail and plan, and never receives your photos or your location. The history keeps the last two hundred exports in the app’s own files.
device.heading: Photos, addresses and history

external.description: To turn latitude and longitude into a readable address, the operating system queries Google's or Apple's geocoding service. That is the only information that leaves, and the system sends it, not the app.
external.heading: Only turning a coordinate into an address

data.note: It is all set out — including what that means under Brazil's LGPD — in the <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy>. Turning off the location permission leaves the app fully functional; only the address field then has to be typed by hand.
data.title: Where your data sits

deleteAccount.deletesNow: Deleting your account immediately erases your email, your identifier, and the record of plan, quota and photo count.
deleteAccount.irreversible: Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. The photos on your device are not affected — they were never on our servers.
deleteAccount.retained: Payment transaction records are retained for the legally required fiscal period, unlinked from your profile. Technical logs expire on their own schedule.
deleteAccount.title: Delete account

site.description: Android app that stamps the time, date, weekday, address and a tracking code onto site-inspection and proof-of-service photos.

desktop.explanation: Your account is ready. Click the button below to open Lymark on your computer already signed in — the browser will ask permission to open the app.
desktop.title: Sign in on desktop
desktop.unavailable: The desktop app connection is not available yet.

address.description: The street type is abbreviated and the state becomes its code, so the address fits in two lines without covering the photo. If you typed before GPS answered, what you typed wins.
address.heading: Filled in by GPS, correctable by hand

code.description: It exists so you can cite one specific photo in a work order or a report. It runs rotated down the right edge, or sits with the data block — your choice.
code.heading: Fourteen characters, drawn by a cryptographic generator

features.note: Every field switches on and off on its own, and the block anchors to any of the four corners, in three sizes. The preview uses your actual photo, not a generic sample: what you see on screen is literally what gets exported.

time.description: One button snaps all three fields back to the present when the capture took longer than expected. All of them stay editable.
time.heading: From the device clock, at the moment of capture

features.title: What goes onto the image

footer.description: Lymark — photographic records with date, time and address.

hero.cta: Open the app in your browser
hero.description: Lymark stamps the time, date, weekday, address and a tracking code straight onto the image. The file that comes out of the app carries the information inside it — not as metadata riding alongside, which the first WhatsApp forward strips away.
hero.heading: The photo leaves your phone already saying when, where and what.

capture.description: The address lookup starts the moment the photo comes in. The fields stay open for adjustment while it runs.
capture.heading: Camera or gallery

process.note: The two actions are kept apart on purpose. Saving and sharing solve different problems, and folding them into one button would drag anyone who just wants to file the photo through a send screen.

save.description: It sits with the rest of your phone's photos, available to any app — including after you uninstall Lymark.
save.heading: Goes to the device gallery

share.description: WhatsApp, email, Drive: the destination is chosen by the operating system, and the app takes no part in sending.
share.heading: Opens the system share sheet

process.title: The path a photo takes

site.title: Lymark — date, time and address watermark for field photos

verify.caveat: The seal attests to the file's integrity and the moment of issuance. What the stamp declares — address, date, time — is the issuer's declaration.
verify.declarationNote: What the stamp shows (address, date, time) is the issuer's declaration — the seal attests to integrity and issuance, not content.
verify.intro: Drop or choose a photo exported by Lymark and see instantly whether it is exactly as it left the app — and who issued it, when.
verify.noSealBody: This file has no Lymark seal. It may have been exported offline, before the seal existed, or may not come from Lymark. Absence of a seal does not prove tampering.
verify.privacyNote: Verification happens in your browser. The file is not sent to any server.
verify.sealedBody: This file is exactly as it left Lymark. Issued by account {account} on {date}.
verify.tamperedBody: The content does not match the seal: the file was modified after issuance, or the seal belongs to another file.
verify.title: Verify authenticity
verify.unsupported: This browser does not support signature verification. Try a current browser.
